name: Groundnut Stem Rot (Sclerotium)
description: A soil-borne fungal disease causing stem rot, wilting, and plant death in groundnut. It is favored by warm temperatures and high soil moisture, forming characteristic white fungal growth and sclerotia on infected tissues.
symptoms: Yellowing and wilting of individual branches or entire plant
White fungal mycelium visible on stems near soil line
Small tan to brown seed-like sclerotia on infected tissue
Plant death in circular patches in the field
causes: High soil moisture and poor drainage
Excessive plant residues on soil surface
treatments: Apply fungicides containing tebuconazole or flutolanil to soil at pegging stage
Remove and destroy infected plants with surrounding soil
prevention: Practice crop rotation with cereals or grasses
Ensure well-drained fields and avoid waterlogging
Plant on ridges or raised beds to improve drainage
Deep plow to bury crop debris
Reduce plant density for better aeration
